launch.name: Work Orca
launch.summary: Orca on the default profile (%APPDATA%\orca), full screen 1, holding the work repos that `devenv orca apply` registers. Replaces the Workspace Terminal columns. Listed before Personal Orca so a fresh logon launches it first: each launch waits for a window that was not open before it, so the two Orca windows cannot swap. On a re-run `window_pid_file` picks the window owned by the pid this profile records in orca-runtime.json.

launch.name: Personal Orca
launch.summary: Orca on a second profile (`--user-data-dir`), full screen 2, holding the personal repos that `rig estate orca --apply` registers. Orca is one window per profile, so a second window needs a second profile. Orca's in-app update relaunches only the profile that ran it, so rig applies updates instead: restore installs a staged update while no Orca is running, and `desktop-manager workspace update-orca` closes both profiles, installs and relaunches both. If an in-app update closes this one anyway, the next restore finds no orca-runtime.json pid for it and launches it.
